newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Treasury confident NZ growth up towards forecast.
newsitem.headline: Treasury confident NZ growth up towards forecast.

text.p: New Zealand Treasury Secretary Murray Horn said on Wednesday he was confident that 1996/97 economic growth would be up towards Treasury's forecasts.
In its December Economic and Fiscal Update, Treasury forecast annual average economic growth of 2.6 percent in the year to March 1997.
Horn, speaking at parliament's finance and expenditure committee, referred to a market consensus forecast of 1.8 percent growth for the period.
"If you are looking at the current year, 96/7, we are expecting that consensus, which is about 1.8 percent, lower than ours, to come up," Horn said.
He said that the September quarter GDP outcome was higher than the consensus forecast.
"On the basis of the September outcome, the December and March quarters have to be pretty much flat for the consensus to come true," he said.
Horn added that figures for the December quarter showed that exports were coming through strongly while imports remained flat. He said the consumption cycle was very similar to Treasury's forecasts.
